cues: With and, the subject is plural: Sita and Gita are cousins.
But if the two words name one thing, the verb is singular: bread and butter is a cheap breakfast.
Each and every keep it singular: every boy and every girl was given a badge.
As well as, along with and together with only add information, so the verb agrees with the first subject: the captain, as well as the players, was praised.
And with either or, neither nor, not only but also, and plain or, the verb agrees with the nearer subject.
